newsitem.title: USA: Pentagon chief disappointed by base closings vote.
newsitem.headline: Pentagon chief disappointed by base closings vote.

text.p: U.S. Defense Secretary William Cohen was disappointed at a two-to-one vote in the U.S. Senate to delay closing military bases, a Pentagon spokesman said on Thursday.

The Senate voted late on Wednesday to postpone any base closings until 2001. If enacted into law, this would have a major impact on long-range Defense Department plans to modernize and streamline operations, spokesman Capt. Michael Doubleday said at a briefing.
"The secretary was certainly disappointed with the action that was taken in the Senate," Doubleday said. Cohen was traveling in Europe on Thursday.

Doubleday noted that Cohen had been working hard to cut out unnecessary infrastructure in the department and had called for two more rounds of base closures in 1999 and 2001, partly to help pay for billions of dollars in high-tech weaponry for the 21st century. Cohen estimated those base closings would save about $2.7 billion a year.
The Senate voted to delay the next round until early in 2001, pending further analysis by the Pentagon and government economists of how much the closures actually save.
The House previously passed its version of the defense bill, omitting the authorization of base closings.
Doubleday said the Pentagon had already decreased force structure by 33 percent. However, he said domestic infrastructure -- including military bases -- had declined only 21 percent so far.
"We simply can't afford a waste of resources in an environment where we've got a lot of tough choices and fiscal constraints," Doubleday said.
He said the department would work on the analysis of actual savings from base closings required in the Senate-passed legislation.
